polish.quote: Depend only on OWN-DATA-STORE; implement every documented decision, failure, cancellation, cleanup, and recovery branch.
polish.why: No struct, constructor or method signature is given for LifecycleCoordinator. It does not say how it receives the Option<Arc<DataStore>>, how it registers close-request and SIGTERM handlers, or what 'cancel active tasks' cancels. The agent must invent this API.
polish.fix: Add a short interface to TASK-03: LifecycleCoordinator::new(store: Option<Arc<DataStore>>), shutdown(&self) that closes the store if present, and where app.rs calls it from the window close-request and SIGTERM handlers.

polish.why: The activate handler builds a new window on every activation. The lifecycle contract requires exactly one primary window and reopening from the launcher, and no task may edit main.rs (TASK-01 says to verify the kit files unchanged).
polish.fix: Tell TASK-03 to make build_window return the existing application.active_window() when one exists, so main.rs stays unchanged.

polish.why: TASKS.md TASK-05 says to store the ToastOverlay, timer state, loaded records and status in 'the shared view state'. A GTK widget handle cannot live in this serde/Eq-derived AppState, and the packet does not say whether to add a new type.
polish.fix: State in TASK-05 that the view state is a new non-serde struct in src/state.rs, with the overlay held as an Option so display-free tests can construct it.

polish.why: The struct derives Default and build_services uses Services::default(). After TASK-02 and TASK-04 it holds Option<Arc<DataStore>> and Arc<PermissionCoordinator>. The Arc field only derives Default if PermissionCoordinator implements it, and a real owner should not be built through a default.
polish.fix: In TASK-02, tell the agent to drop derive(Default) and construct Services explicitly in build_services.

polish.quote: when the store's list returns Err the label shows 0.
polish.why: The label text format is never given (bare number or captioned). No display-free function is named that tests can assert for 'displayed count', and no mechanism is named by which the shared reload() updates the label.
polish.fix: Specify the label text (for example 'Sessions today: N'), a display-free fn count_label(count: usize) -> String, and a reload callback that sets the label.

polish.quote: a today-count slot (an empty gtk::Box directly under the MM:SS display)
polish.why: The same prompt later lists the layout as 'a row of Start, Pause and Reset buttons sized to their labels, the today-count slot and the status area'. This puts the slot after the buttons, so the vertical order is stated two ways.
polish.fix: State one order, for example MM:SS, today-count slot, buttons, status area.

polish.quote: the status area shows 'Desktop notifications are unavailable.' and nothing is retried
polish.why: Nothing says when the status text is cleared. It would stay forever after a later Start or Reset, and a later successful notification would still show the stale message.
polish.fix: Add: clear the status area on Start and Reset and on a successful notify.

polish.why: The notify call (with its synchronous D-Bus probe) is made from the completion path. If that runs on the GTK main thread, it blocks the UI for up to 500 ms, which breaks the 'No blocking I/O runs on the main thread' rule. The packet does not say which thread calls notify. gio::Application is also not Send.
polish.fix: State that notify is called on the main thread and that the probe result is cached at startup, or run the probe via spawn_blocking before the call.

review.verdict: No blocking defects found. The packet maps every idea sentence to a feature and a testable acceptance criterion. The task order, owner maps and shared-file lists agree, and the data and time rules are unambiguous (the day-bounds test vector checks out). The remaining items are underspecified details that a competent coder can resolve.
